questions.stem: Which text type opens with « Cher journal, » and records the writer's own day?
options: a formal letter
a report
a brochure
a journal entry
questions.explanation: A journal entry is personal writing in the first person, often addressed to the diary itself. A formal letter would open with « Madame, Monsieur, ».

questions.stem: Which is the French way to write the place and date at the head of a letter?
options: « Melbourne, 3 Mai »
« Melbourne, le 3 mai »
« Melbourne, mai le 3 »
« Le 3ème Mai, Melbourne »
questions.explanation: French writes the place, a comma, then « le » with the day before the month, and months take no capital. « Le 3ème Mai » copies English order with a capital and an ordinal French does not use for dates other than the first.

questions.stem: In an email, what goes after « Objet : »?
options: the subject line
the recipient's address
the attachment
the signature
questions.explanation: « L'objet » of an email or formal letter is its subject. The recipient goes after « À : ».

questions.stem: In a newspaper or magazine article, what is « le chapeau »?
options: the caption printed under a photograph
the short paragraph under the headline
the headline at the top of the page
the photo of the journalist who wrote it
questions.explanation: « Le chapeau » sums up the article in a few lines between the headline (« le titre ») and the body. Using a title and a chapeau shows awareness of the article's layout.

questions.stem: Which feature most clearly marks a film review, « une critique »?
options: a greeting and a formal closing formula
a list of facts with no opinions at all
a personal evaluation with a recommendation
a set of numbered instructions to follow in order
questions.explanation: A review informs readers about the film and then judges it, often ending with a recommendation such as « à ne pas manquer ». A formal closing formula belongs to a letter.

questions.stem: Which feature best marks a report, « un rapport »?
options: a first-person account of the writer's own feelings and hopes
a story told in the past historic and imperfect
an impersonal tone, with headings and recommendations
a chatty tone, with questions to the reader
questions.explanation: A report presents findings objectively, often with phrases such as « il ressort que » or « il convient de », and ends with recommendations. Personal feelings belong to a journal entry or personal letter.

questions.stem: Which opening suits a speech to a school assembly?
options: « Objet : discours pour l'assemblée du lycée »
« Il était une fois, dans un lycée lointain… »
« Mesdames et Messieurs, chers camarades, »
« Cher journal, aujourd'hui c'est le grand jour… »
questions.explanation: A speech addresses its audience directly at the start. « Il était une fois » opens a fairy tale, and « Objet : » belongs to an email or formal letter.

questions.stem: Which language feature suits a tourist brochure?
options: a personal greeting and a formal closing formula at the end
imperatives addressed to the reader, such as « Découvrez… »
past historic verbs that narrate a sequence of events
headings such as « Conclusions et recommandations »
questions.explanation: Brochures persuade and inform at once, so they speak to the reader with imperatives and appealing adjectives. Conclusions and recommendations belong to a report.

questions.stem: Which text type uses stage directions, « les didascalies »?
options: a report on a school excursion
a review of a new novel
an article for a newspaper
a script for a play or film
questions.explanation: Stage directions tell actors how to move or speak and are written in italics or brackets. A script is one of the text types students may produce.

questions.stem: Which feature is typical of a blog post?
options: a conversational tone that invites readers' comments
a formal salutation at the top and a closing formula at the end
numbered sections ending in recommendations
stage directions written in brackets
questions.explanation: A blog is personal and informal, addressed to an audience of readers who may reply. Numbered sections ending in recommendations describe a report.

questions.stem: Which writing style aims to convince the reader to adopt a position?
options: informative
imaginative
personal
persuasive
questions.explanation: Persuasive writing argues for a position and tries to move the reader to agree or act. Informative writing presents facts without trying to win the reader over.

questions.stem: Which writing style weighs up different positions before reaching a justified conclusion?
options: imaginative
personal
evaluative
persuasive
questions.explanation: Evaluative writing compares positions fairly and then justifies a conclusion. Persuasive writing starts from one position and argues for it.

questions.stem: Which sentence best fits an informative piece rather than a persuasive one?
options: « Vous ne pouvez absolument pas manquer ce festival extraordinaire, croyez-moi ! »
« Qui n'a jamais rêvé de passer un été comme celui-là, au soleil ? »
« Il est grand temps que la ville soutienne enfin ce festival unique. »
« Le festival a lieu chaque année en juillet et attire de nombreux visiteurs. »
questions.explanation: It states facts in a neutral tone. The others use an exclamation and intensifiers, a rhetorical question, and a call for action, all persuasive devices.

questions.stem: What most distinguishes imaginative writing?
options: it records the writer's real experiences and feelings
it invents characters, settings or events
it presents verifiable facts in an impersonal register
it weighs up arguments before reaching a conclusion
questions.explanation: Imaginative writing invents its content, such as a short story or a scene for a script. Recording real experiences and feelings is personal writing.

questions.stem: In French dialogue, how is a change of speaker usually shown?
options: a new set of single quotation marks on each line
the new speaker's words printed in italics
a dash at the start of the new speaker's line
the speaker's name in capitals before each line
questions.explanation: French prose often opens a dialogue with guillemets and marks each change of speaker with a dash (—) on a new line. Names in capitals before each line belong to a script.

questions.stem: Which is punctuated and ordered correctly?
options: « Je pars demain, elle dit. »
« Je pars demain, dit elle. »
« Je pars demain, elle a dit-elle. »
« Je pars demain, dit-elle. »
questions.explanation: After direct speech, the verb of saying and its subject are inverted and joined with a hyphen: « dit-elle », « répondit-il ». « Elle dit » keeps English order.

questions.stem: Léa said « Je viendrai demain ». Which form completes « Léa a dit qu'elle ___ le lendemain. »?
options: viendra
était venue
vienne
viendrait
questions.explanation: When the reporting verb is in the past, a future in the original becomes a conditional: « je viendrai » becomes « elle viendrait ». « Viendra » would keep the tense of the original words.

questions.stem: Max asked « Est-ce que tu as fini ? ». Which word completes « Max m'a demandé ___ j'avais fini. »?
options: est-ce que
si
que
ce que
questions.explanation: A yes/no question is reported with « si » ('whether'). « Est-ce que » belongs to direct questions and disappears in reported speech.

questions.stem: Inès asked « Qu'est-ce que tu veux ? ». Which words complete « Inès m'a demandé ___ je voulais. »?
options: ce que
qu'est-ce que
que
quoi
questions.explanation: In reported speech « qu'est-ce que » becomes « ce que », and « qu'est-ce qui » becomes « ce qui ». Keeping « qu'est-ce que » leaves a direct question inside a statement.

questions.stem: In reported speech set in the past, what does « demain » usually become?
options: « la veille »
« la semaine suivante »
« le lendemain »
« hier »
questions.explanation: Time words shift with the point of view: « demain » becomes « le lendemain » and « hier » becomes « la veille ». « La veille » is the day before, the opposite direction.

questions.stem: The teacher said « Taisez-vous ! » to the class. Which words complete « Le prof nous a dit ___. »?
options: de nous taire
de vous taire
nous taire
que taisez-vous
questions.explanation: A reported command uses « dire de » plus an infinitive, and the pronoun shifts to match the speakers: the teacher's « vous » becomes our « nous ». « De vous taire » forgets that shift.

questions.stem: In careful written French, Tom said « J'ai perdu mes clés ». Which form completes « Tom a dit qu'il ___ ses clés. »?
options: avait perdu
a perdu
perdrait
aurait perdu
questions.explanation: A passé composé in the original moves back to the pluperfect after a past reporting verb, since the loss came before the saying. « Perdrait » would turn it into a future event.

questions.stem: Writing to the parents of a host family you have not yet met, which form of address is right?
options: on throughout
vous throughout
tu throughout
tu at first, then vous
questions.explanation: Adults you do not know are addressed as « vous », and switching mid-letter would be inconsistent. « Tu » is for friends, family and people of your own age.

questions.stem: Which word needs a capital letter in French?
options: the month in « je pars en janvier »
the noun in « les australiens aiment le sport »
the adjective in « le drapeau australien »
the language in « elle parle anglais »
questions.explanation: A noun for a person of a nationality takes a capital, « les Australiens », but French does not capitalise adjectives of nationality, languages, days or months. English capitalises all four, which is the source of the error.

questions.stem: Which is the more formal equivalent of « un boulot » for a job application?
options: « un petit job »
« un taf »
« un truc »
« un emploi »
questions.explanation: « Un emploi » or « un poste » suits a formal letter. « Taf » and « job » are informal, like « boulot » itself.

questions.stem: Which sentence is in a formal register?
options: « Tu peux m'envoyer une brochure sur ton lycée, s'il te plaît ? »
« Envoie-moi vite une brochure, merci d'avance ! »
« Ce serait trop cool d'avoir une brochure sur vos cours de langue, non ? »
« Je vous serais reconnaissant de bien vouloir m'envoyer une brochure. »
questions.explanation: The conditional, « vous » and the set phrase « bien vouloir » mark a formal request. « Tu peux… s'il te plaît » is polite but informal.

questions.stem: Which set of connectives takes an evaluative essay from start to finish in order?
options: « En revanche… Ensuite… Pour conclure… Tout d'abord… »
« Tout d'abord… Ensuite… En revanche… Pour conclure… »
« Pour conclure… Tout d'abord… En revanche… Ensuite… »
« Ensuite… Pour conclure… Tout d'abord… En revanche… »
questions.explanation: « Tout d'abord » opens, « ensuite » adds, « en revanche » introduces the other side, and « pour conclure » closes. Sequencing ideas logically is a key skill in both evaluative and persuasive writing.

questions.stem: Which phrase concedes a point before countering it?
options: « Certes…, mais… »
« De plus… »
« Par conséquent… »
« C'est-à-dire… »
questions.explanation: « Certes » ('admittedly') grants the other side a point, and « mais » turns back to the writer's view. « Par conséquent » introduces a result, not a concession.

questions.stem: What does « en revanche » signal in an argument?
options: an example of the previous point
a repetition of the previous point
a contrast with the previous point
a consequence of the previous point
questions.explanation: « En revanche » means 'on the other hand'. Although « la revanche » means revenge, the phrase has nothing to do with retaliation.

questions.stem: Which sentence draws a justified conclusion in an evaluative piece?
options: « Achetez-le dès aujourd'hui, vous ne le regretterez jamais, c'est promis ! »
« Certains pensent que c'est utile, d'autres non, voilà tout. »
« Je trouve ça génial, et c'est mon dernier mot là-dessus. »
« Tout bien considéré, les avantages l'emportent, surtout pour les jeunes. »
questions.explanation: « Tout bien considéré » signals a conclusion after weighing both sides, and « surtout pour les jeunes » justifies it. Listing views with « voilà tout » reaches no conclusion at all.

questions.stem: Which persuasive device is used in « Agir, c'est possible. Agir, c'est urgent. Agir, c'est notre devoir. »?
options: an exaggerated comparison with something else
a question to which the answer is obvious
a quotation from an expert
repetition of an opening word for emphasis
questions.explanation: Repeating « agir » at the start of each sentence (anaphora) builds rhythm and insistence. There is no question here, rhetorical or otherwise.

questions.stem: Why might a persuasive speech use « nous » and « notre » often?
options: to include the audience in a shared responsibility
to show the speaker is talking about a group of experts
to make the speech sound more formal and distant
to avoid having to state any opinion directly
questions.explanation: Inclusive « nous » puts speaker and audience on the same side, which makes a call to action harder to refuse. It brings the audience closer rather than creating distance.

questions.stem: In a story, which tense sets the scene and describes background, such as weather and feelings?
options: the future
the conditional
the present subjunctive
the imperfect
questions.explanation: The imperfect describes ongoing states and background, while the passé composé, or the past historic in literary writing, moves the events forward.

questions.stem: « Il pleuvait depuis des heures. Soudain, quelqu'un a frappé à la porte. » Why does the tense change?
options: The imperfect is used for weather; the passé composé for anything about people
The imperfect is literary; the passé composé is used for spoken French only
The imperfect sets an ongoing background; the passé composé marks a sudden event
The imperfect is used for the distant past; the passé composé for the recent past
questions.explanation: The rain was going on when one completed action interrupted it, and « soudain » signals that. The choice is about aspect, not about how long ago it happened.

questions.stem: In a bilingual dictionary, what does « nf » after a French word tell you?
options: it is a verb with no object
it is a feminine noun
it is a noun with no plural
it is informal French
questions.explanation: « n » is « nom » (noun) and « f » is « féminin ». Checking this before writing avoids errors with articles and agreements.

questions.stem: You look up 'book' in order to write 'I booked a table'. Why is « un livre » wrong?
options: « Livre » is only used in Québec, not in France
'Book' is a verb here, and « livre » is the noun for a book
« Livre » is a false friend that actually means 'free' in French
« Livre » is feminine, so it cannot be used with « table »
questions.explanation: A dictionary entry lists several parts of speech; 'to book' a table is « réserver ». Checking the part of speech is one of the self-correcting strategies the study design names.

questions.stem: Chloé said « Je suis arrivée hier ». Which sentence reports it in careful written French?
options: « Chloé a dit qu'elle était arrivée la veille. »
« Chloé a dit qu'elle est arrivée hier. »
« Chloé a dit qu'elle était arrivée le lendemain. »
« Chloé a dit qu'elle arriverait la veille. »
questions.explanation: Two things shift: the passé composé moves back to the pluperfect, and « hier » becomes « la veille », the day before. « Le lendemain » is the day after, the opposite direction.

questions.stem: You are writing a 300-word evaluative piece on screen time. Which plan suits the style?
options: introduce the issue, weigh both sides, then justify a conclusion
argue for one side throughout and end with a call to action
tell the story of a character who cannot put down a phone
describe your own week of screen use in the form of a diary
questions.explanation: Evaluative writing compares positions before reaching a justified conclusion. Arguing one side and ending with a call to action is persuasive writing, and the others are imaginative and personal.

questions.stem: In a persuasive piece, what is « Imaginez un monde sans plastique… » doing?
options: reporting a fact about pollution
conceding a point to the other side
recounting a past personal experience
inviting readers to picture a hypothetical outcome
questions.explanation: The imperative « imaginez » asks readers to picture a possible future, one of the persuasive strategies the study design names. Nothing in it is presented as fact.

questions.stem: Which sentence would open the body of a formal letter of complaint?
options: « Coucou ! Tu ne devineras jamais ce qui m'est arrivé à l'hôtel la semaine dernière. »
« Il était une fois une cliente très mécontente qui avait réservé une chambre d'hôtel. »
« Je me permets de vous écrire afin de vous faire part de mon mécontentement. »
« Je t'écris vite fait pour te raconter le week-end catastrophique que j'ai passé. »
questions.explanation: « Je me permets de vous écrire » and « faire part de » are formal set phrases, and « vous » suits a company. The others use « tu », a casual greeting or a story opening.

questions.stem: You are writing to Mme Dupont, the director of a language school. Which salutation is correct?
options: « Bonjour Dupont, »
« Madame la Directrice, »
« Chère Mme Dupont, »
« Salut Madame, »
questions.explanation: Formal French letters address the reader by title, « Madame la Directrice », and never put the surname after « Madame » in the salutation. « Chère » is kept for people you know, and « salut » is informal.
